# Quantum Computing

Understand pure qubit states, measurement, unitary gates, Bell entanglement and interference using very small vectors.

**Start with the smallest possible example**, calculate a concrete result, explain every symbol, and then examine the assumptions and limitations.

Quantum computing is a separate interdisciplinary topic under this requested navigation. The first four chapters use ideal mathematical circuits; actual processors have noise and hardware-specific constraints.

## Four lessons

1. [Qubits and Measurement](01-qubits-and-measurement.qmd)
2. [Gates and Matrices](02-gates-and-matrices.qmd)
3. [Entanglement and Bell States](03-entanglement-and-bell-states.qmd)
4. [Circuits and Sampling](04-quantum-circuits-and-sampling.qmd)

## After these lessons

Explain the core example without memorising definitions. Change one assumption and predict what changes in the result. The purpose is to understand the system, not collect terminology.
